payload.title: Are Lab-Grown Diamonds Worth It?
payload.excerpt: Lab-grown diamonds are real diamonds. What is the same, what differs (origin, disclosure, value, sentiment) and when lab-grown is worth it for you.
key_takeaways: A lab-grown diamond is real diamond with essentially the same physical, chemical and optical properties as a mined one, while cubic zirconia and moissanite are not diamond at all.
Since 1 October 2025, GIA describes colourless lab-grown diamonds as "Premium" or "Standard" rather than on the colour and clarity scales it uses for natural stones.
Origin must be disclosed clearly, so look for "laboratory-grown" or "lab-created" next to the word "diamond" on the receipt, the report and the girdle inscription.
Lab-grown is worth it if you value the look and want the rest of your plans to have room, and worth a second thought if rarity, origin and an heirloom story matter most to you.

faq.q: Is a lab-grown diamond a real diamond?
faq.a: Yes. It has the same crystal structure as a natural diamond and nearly the same chemical, optical and physical properties; only its growth history differs.

faq.q: Can a jeweller tell if a diamond is lab-grown?
faq.a: Not by eye. Separating them needs screening equipment and advanced spectroscopic testing at a lab such as GIA. An inscription and a verified report are the everyday proof.

faq.q: Do lab-grown diamonds hold their value?
faq.a: Treat neither lab-grown nor natural as an investment. If resale matters, ask the seller about buy-back or upgrade terms and get them in writing before you buy.

faq.q: Are lab-grown diamonds legal to sell in Australia?
faq.a: Our research found no Australian restriction specific to lab-grown diamonds. As at October 2026, no ACCC guidance specific to lab-grown diamonds was found, and the general Australian Consumer Law rule applies: claims must be accurate, truthful and based on reasonable grounds. This is general information, not legal advice.

faq.q: Is a lab-grown diamond the same as cubic zirconia or moissanite?
faq.a: No. Cubic zirconia and moissanite are simulants, unrelated to diamond at the atomic level, while a lab-grown diamond is diamond.

faq.q: How do I know if my lab-grown diamond is CVD or HPHT?
faq.a: A lab can tell: GIA determines the growth method with spectroscopy and other testing. GIA's reports for lab-grown coloured diamonds include growth type; for a colourless stone, ask the seller whether the report states it.
